misconceptions.description: Submitting peer feedback that is mostly encouragement ('great job, very clear') with no actionable, evidence-based observation
misconceptions.trigger: review consists of compliments and a rating with no specific design issue
misconceptions.feedback: A scholarly critique names a specific element, the problem with it, and a criterion or principle behind the judgment. Praise is not critique.

misconceptions.description: Phrasing critique as personal preference ('I would have used blue') instead of tying it to a shared rubric, principle, or learner outcome
misconceptions.trigger: feedback uses 'I don't like' with no criterion the author can act on objectively
misconceptions.feedback: Reframe preferences as criteria: name the alignment, usability, or accessibility standard, so the author can judge the point on its merits.

misconceptions.description: Receiving peer critique and either accepting every comment or dismissing it wholesale, rather than recording a reasoned accept, modify, or reject disposition for each point
misconceptions.trigger: author makes all suggested edits or none, with no rationale logged per comment
misconceptions.feedback: Log a disposition for each comment: accept, modify, or reject, with the reason. Peer review informs judgment; it does not replace it.

misconceptions.description: Submitting AI-generated critique of a peer's work as your own review without verifying that the issues are real and present in the artifact
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes an AI critique that flags problems not actually in the peer's prototype
misconceptions.feedback: If you use AI to draft critique, verify each issue against the peer's actual artifact before submitting; an unchecked AI review can fabricate problems.
